<reflection>
Top mechanisms remain M17, M16, M7 — all involving second-order effects with catS. M18 and M12 are close behind:
- M17: P + catS => inactive (product deactivation)
- M16: S + catS => inactive (substrate deactivation)
- M7: catS2 productive intermediate
- M18: 2catS => inactive (catS dimerization)
- M12: P + cat => inactive

Adding product improved fit for M17 but M16 also improved similarly. The three top mechanisms have different substrate/product dependencies:
- M16 rate loss ∝ [S][catS], so higher [S] → faster deactivation
- M17 rate loss ∝ [P][catS], so higher [P] → faster deactivation
- M7 has no deactivation, just alternative pathway; higher [S] → more catS2

To discriminate, need a high substrate experiment with low product. M16 should show incomplete conversion. M7 should show enhanced rate. M17 should behave normally (product builds up slowly initially).
</reflection>
<hypothesis>
Propose high substrate, low catalyst, no product:
- **M16**: Fast irreversible deactivation via S+catS → little product formed, plateaus early with low final conversion
- **M17**: Product accumulates but slowly initially → higher initial rate, deactivation only when P builds up → moderate/high conversion, mid curvature
- **M7**: catS2 productive → enhanced rate at high [S], approaches full conversion smoothly
- **M18**: 2catS dimerization deactivation → depends on [catS]² so low cat concentration mitigates → moderate deactivation
- **M12**: P+cat deactivation → similar to M17 but at free cat

Use high S (4.0) and low cat (0.005) to amplify [S][catS] deactivation vs [catS]² effects.
</hypothesis>
